lawyer: Md. Ahsanul Kabir, Advocate — For the Petitioner.
parties:
Kali Joy Dey ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Anjana Rani Dhar and others ----- Opposite Parties
full_judgment:
The defendant has moved this revisional application under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure calling in question the order dated 19-2-95 passed by the Assistant Judge, Feni, in Civil Suit No. 54 of 1994 (A suit for declaration that a Kabala said to have been executed on 10-4-63 by their predecessor Madhusudan is illegal, void and not binding upon the plaintiff rejecting an application filed by the petitioner under Order 7 rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejection of the plaint on the ground that the suit is barred by limitation and it is undervalued. 

 2. The learned Advocate for the petitioner has strenuously argued that in the absence of any specific provision in the Limitation Act providing for specific period of limitation for seeking declaration that the . certain kabala is illegal, void without consideration and not binding upon the plaintiff, etc. the period mentioned in Article 121 of the Limitation Act shall be made applicable and such period shall run for six years from the date of accrual of the right to sue which period having expired long before the institution of the suit on 1-8-94, the learned trial Judge acted illegally in. refusing to reject the plaint under section 3 of the Limitation Act. 

 4. The learned Assistant Judge upon consideration of the statements made in the plaint as well as the objection raised by the defendant and after hearing both the parties arrived at a conclusion that both the question of limitation as well as valuation of the suit being the mixed question of law and fact those issues may safely be resolved upon the evidence to be adduced by the respective parties in support of their respective contentions. 

 6. So far the question of limitation is concerned it cannot be said with all certainty at this stage of the suit that the same is barred by limitation in view of the provision of Article 121 of the Limitation Act which warrants its dismissal under section 3 of the Limitation Act. 

 7. In support of his contention the learned Advocate has referred to a decision reported in 20 DLR (WP) 113 in the case of Shafiq Ahmed vs. Mirza Mohammad Anwar Beg. In that case their Lordhips Sardar Muhammad Iqbal and Md. Fazle Ghani Khan JJ, observed that in a suit for cancellation of a sale deed, where the plaint was registered upon fulfillment of the requirement of rule 1 of Order 7, but after issuance of the summons defendant raised a question of limitation and thereby special issue was framed and tried against the plaintiff and the plaint was rejected bringing the analogy that the suit was covered by the provisions of Article 91 of the Limitation Act which provides that cancellation should be sought within 3 years from the right accrued or from the date of knowledge, Thus the cited decision has little to help the petitioner. 

 8. Admittedly, the defendant has not yet filed the written statement in the suit. After raising objection in the written statement the defendant may ask the court for framing special issues either on the point of limitation or on the point of the valuation of the suit and to decide those questions before going into the other points on merit of the suit.
